## Summary
Ids are `BIGINT` identity values exposed directly as FHIR ids, so they are enumerable. Add UUID public ids in a new migration, keep the BIGINT keys internally, and update subject-reference parsing.

## Findings
| id | severity | category | location | evidence | recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARC-001 | medium | security | sample-app/src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__init.sql:3 | `id BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY` is the FHIR id: sequential ids allow enumeration | Add `public_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE` to both tables and expose it as the FHIR id. |
| ARC-002 | high | correctness | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/api/ObservationMapper.java:47 | `parseSubject` does `Long.valueOf(raw)`: a `Patient/3f2c...` reference becomes a 400 | Resolve `Patient/{uuid}` through `PatientRepository.findByPublicId`; accept numeric ids during a deprecation window. |
| ARC-003 | medium | design | sample-app/src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__init.sql:26 | `fk_observation_patient FOREIGN KEY (patient_id) REFERENCES patient (id)` | Keep the BIGINT foreign key; only the external id changes, so `patient_id` and the FK stay as they are. |
| ARC-004 | medium | standards | context/standards/coding-standards.md:12 | Coding-standards rule 10: never edit an applied migration | Ship a new migration `V2__public_ids.sql` with `gen_random_uuid()` backfill; `V1__init.sql` stays untouched. |
